description: We are a team of five computer engineering students passionate about space, technology, AI, and innovation. We enjoy solving real-world problems, learning together, and turning creative ideas into practical solutions. Our skills include software development, AI/ML, data analysis, and problem-solving.
summary: Trend Dedektifi turns scattered NASA Earth observation data into a citable, trust-scored climate trend dataset for all 81 provinces of Türkiye. We harmonize 26 NASA variables (MERRA-2, GLDAS, GPM IMERG, MODIS, GRACE and others, 2001–2025) onto one 0.25° monthly grid, test trends with Theil–Sen and modified Mann–Kendall with false-discovery-rate control, and check variable relationships against physics. Every result carries a “finding scorecard” (high/medium/low/none confidence). A web app lets researchers explore, download and cite the results, and an explainable AI layer answers questions without ever generating numbers: every figure is verified against the analysis output.
details:
Problem: NASA data is open but fragmented (different products, grids and units), and two statistical traps make naive trend maps unreliable: testing thousands of locations produces chance “trends”, and two series that both rise over time look correlated even when unrelated.
What we built: (1) L1, a harmonized data cube; (2) L2/L3, cell-, province- and region-level trends for five seasons with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (q ≤ 0.10) and confidence intervals; (3) L4, physically motivated variable pairs chosen before looking at the data, detrended and tested with autocorrelation-aware block permutation; (4) magnitude tests (Clausius–Clapeyron humidity scaling, water budget with GRACE, snow line); (5) a scorecard of five robustness checks per result, with rules fixed before results were seen.
Key findings: winters in Türkiye warmed by 1.16 °C per decade, significant in 73 of 81 provinces; warmer winters mean less snow in 78 of 78 computable provinces (Türkiye-wide r = −0.90, high confidence).
Validation: our processed series match NASA Giovanni (correlation 1.00).
Tools: Python (xarray, pandas, statsmodels), earthaccess, Streamlit.
